paragraphs: Rabbi Yosi son of Rabbi Shalom.

He is mentioned in the old [Midrash Tehillim, at the beginning of chapter 72](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tehillim.72.1). The annotator הרש״ב already observed there that the reading should be Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Shalom. In Seder HaDorot, the printers confused matters and wrote: ‘Rabbi Yosi ben Shalom said: My father had goats,’ etc. They did not see that the saying ‘My father had goats’ belongs to the preceding entry, Rabbi Yosi ben Dolgai. Here it should read Rabbi Yosi son of Rabbi Shalom, from Shocher Tov. This is clear. Maskil LeEitan did not notice this.[^1]

notes.text: The goats saying appears in [Yoma 39b:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.39b.13), in Rabbi Yosi ben Dolgai’s name. Shocher Tov is another name for Midrash Tehillim.
